title: Why Can't You HUM With Your Nose Pinched? 🤐
description:
Hum, then pinch your nose shut while you keep humming: the hum dies within a second. A hum is your voice with your lips shut, so all of its air has to leave through your nose. Pinch your nose and that air piles up in your mouth and puffs your cheeks, until it pushes back as hard as your lungs push. With no air flowing past your vocal cords, they stop buzzing. Weirder: humming swirls air in and out of the hidden caves behind your face, your sinuses. In small studies a hum aired them out far better than plain breathing, and the air coming out of the nose carried about fifteen times more nitric oxide. Did your hum stop? Yes or no?
